newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called slightly lower tracking IPE.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called slightly lower tracking IPE.

text.p: NYMEX crude was seen edging lower at the open Friday tracking slight losses in Brent futures on London's IPE with no news to provide decisive direction.

"We need news to break us out of this $19.00 to $20.00 range. If we don't get it, we may fail yet again above $20.00," said a New York crude trader, noting spot crude's two attempts at a breakout this past week failed.
Crude was called flat to five cents a barrel lower after June crude ended 30 cents up at $20.03 a barrel Thursday. Refined products were called steady to 0.25 cent a gallon up.
At 0936 EDT, June Brent was off seven cents at $18.34 a barrel on the IPE. May gas oil on the IPE was up $1.50 at $166.25 a tonne and supportive for refined products here.
The United Nations said Friday that a report claiming some of its staff in northern Iraq had been arrested by a Kurdish group is untrue.

The alleged arrests had triggered a late session rally throughout the oil complex Thursday. Dealers were concerned that the incident, if true, could jeopardize the oil-for-food deal Iraq with the United Nations.
On Thursday, May gasoline ended 1.10 cents a gallon higher at 62.84 cents a gallon while May heating oil ended 0.24 cent up at 55.89 cents a gallon.
Dealers noted the options expiry in the May refined product contracts may influence late session action with the calls in both gasoline and heating oil having the most open interest.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
